chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Shaybani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to us, from his paternal uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfili, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And He made it a word remaining in his descendants»
He said: It is the Imamate; Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, made it remaining in the descendants of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) until the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What does the 'remaining word' in the descendants of Ibrahim refer to according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explicitly identifies the 'remaining word' (al-kalima al-baqiya) as the Imamate, anchoring its perpetual continuity specifically within the progeny of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him). This interpretation underscores the Shia theological emphasis on the hereditary nature of spiritual authority and distinguishes the enduring legacy of the Ahl al-Bayt from the broader lineage of Ibrahim. The hadith serves as a foundational proof for the permanence of divine guidance through the Imams until the Day of Judgment.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Ahmad al-Shaybani, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Abi Abdillah al-Kufi, that he said: We were told by Musa bin Imran al-Nakha’I, from his paternal uncle, Hussain bin Yazid al-Nawfili, from Hasan bin Ali bin Abi Hamza, from his father, from Abu Baseer, that he said: I asked Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him,
about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And He made it a word that remains in his descendants.» [43:28]
He said: It is Imamate; Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, made it remaining in the descendants of Hussain, peace be upon him, until the Day of Resurrection.
